dashboard.title: System Overview
dashboard.description: Aeon Data Systems is a forensic recovery and secure data-destruction tool. Use The Hunter to scan a storage device for deleted or hidden files, and The Oblivion to permanently destroy sensitive data beyond recovery. Start by selecting a storage device from the left sidebar.
dashboard.startScanDesc: Recover deleted files via sector-level carving

hunter.title: The Hunter — Forensic Recovery
hunter.description: Reads the selected device sector by sector, searching for JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, ZIP, DOC, EXE, MP4, MP3, AVI, RAR and SQLite file signatures. Deleted or hidden files are listed below for recovery.

oblivion.title: The Oblivion — Secure Data Shredder
oblivion.description: Permanently destroys data by overwriting it multiple times so it cannot be recovered, even with forensic tools. Works on individual files or entire drives. Select a target below to get started.

DoD5220.name: DoD 5220.22-M
DoD5220.forWhom: Use this if you are not sure which to pick. Works on files, USB drives, and hard disks (HDD).
DoD5220.desc: Overwrites your data 3 times in sequence: first with all zeros, then with all ones, then with random data. This is the official standard of the US Department of Defense. It takes a few minutes per gigabyte and leaves no recoverable trace.

Gutmann35.name: Gutmann 35-Pass
Gutmann35.recommendation: 🔬 Extreme — only for old hard disks
Gutmann35.forWhom: Only useful for very old magnetic hard drives (pre-2000). Do NOT use on SSD, NVMe, or USB drives — it does not add any security and takes hours.
Gutmann35.desc: Overwrites data 35 times using specific bit patterns designed for older hard disk technology. On modern drives and SSDs it offers no advantage over DoD 5220.22-M. Choose this only if you need maximum assurance on an old HDD. Expect several hours per gigabyte.

RandomSingle.name: Random (1 Pass)
RandomSingle.recommendation: ⚡ Fastest — ideal for SSDs and quick wipes
RandomSingle.forWhom: Use this for SSD drives, NVMe drives, USB flash drives, or when you need to delete a file quickly. Also the best choice for individual files.
RandomSingle.desc: Overwrites data once with completely random bytes generated by a secure algorithm (ChaCha20). For SSD and flash drives, a single random pass is enough — the way these drives work makes multi-pass approaches pointless. Very fast: typically a few seconds to a couple of minutes per gigabyte.

NvmeSanitize.name: NVMe Sanitize
NvmeSanitize.forWhom: Use this to wipe an entire NVMe or M.2 SSD drive completely. Requires running as Administrator. Enter a device path like \\.\PhysicalDrive0.
NvmeSanitize.desc: Sends a special command directly to the SSD's internal chip, telling its own hardware to erase every memory cell — including hidden areas that software normally cannot reach. This is the most complete wipe possible for an SSD. Does not work on regular files or HDDs.

NvmeFormat.name: NVMe Format NVM
NvmeFormat.recommendation: 🔧 Alternative when Sanitize is not available
NvmeFormat.forWhom: Use this if NVMe Sanitize does not work on your drive. Also requires Administrator and a device path like \\.\PhysicalDrive0.
NvmeFormat.desc: Sends a Format command directly to the NVMe drive's hardware, erasing and resetting the entire storage namespace. Slightly faster than Sanitize on some drives. Use this as a fallback if the Sanitize option returns an error.

complete.body: All passes finished successfully. If this was a file, it has been deleted. The data cannot be recovered.

error.title: Operation failed
error.hint: Common causes: the path does not exist, you need to run as Administrator (required for device paths), or the drive is currently in use by another program.

wipe.title: Free Space Cleaner
wipe.description: Covers the traces of files you deleted the normal way (Recycle Bin, Delete key) weeks or months ago. Those old files are still physically on the disk until something overwrites them — this does exactly that. It fills all free space with random data and then removes the temporary file, leaving your free space the same size but unreadable by recovery tools.
wipe.placeholder: C:\  or  D:\  (the drive to clean)
wipe.browseTitle: Select the folder or drive to clean
wipe.warning: All free space on the drive containing "{{path}}" will be filled with random data. This takes several minutes and the disk will appear almost full during the process — that is normal. When it finishes, the temporary file is deleted and your free space returns to normal.
wipe.confirm: I understand — start overwriting free space
wipe.progress: Overwriting free space with random data…
wipe.completeBytes: of random data written and cleared
